findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): approval does not propagate to delegated payment task

attack_path.note: Trusted purchase request starts the workflow.
Approval covers only item and budget before quotes exist and is not passed onward.
Untrusted vendor quote supplies bank details and quote content.
Orchestrator delegates payment details to payments-agent, which pays the bank details in the task.
Peer agent trusts orchestrator bearer token and performs payment without original approval context.

threat_refs.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Direct Agent Communication

evidence.observation: The manager approves item and budget before any quote exists, and the approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
The orchestrator is instructed to choose a quote, use the bank details from the chosen quote, and rely on payments-agent for remaining checks.
The peer exposes a pay_vendor skill over A2A authenticated by bearer token.

recommendations.action: Propagate the manager approval context, approved amount, approved vendor identity, and allowed payment destination to payments-agent and reject delegated payments that lack or exceed that bound record.
Require recipient and bank details to resolve from an approved vendor master record rather than from quote text supplied by email.

forecast.watch_signal: Any new delegated payment peer or workflow change that continues to omit bound approval context should trigger reassessment.

findings.title: Supply-chain and spoofing exposure: payments-agent card is neither signed nor pinned

attack_path.note: Remote peer is selected from fetched agent card metadata.
Agent card is fetched at startup and cached without signature or pinning.
Delegated payment action depends on the peer definition and endpoint fetched from that card.

evidence.observation: The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
The orchestrator consumes URL and skill metadata from the peer agent card.
payments-agent is relied on to pay delegated bank details, so poisoned peer metadata affects an irreversible payment path.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin the payments-agent card or endpoint identity, and reject unpinned or changed definitions until reapproved.

forecast.watch_signal: Agent card URL, endpoint identity, or accepted peer list changes without a pin or signature check.

findings.title: Missing attributable record for delegated payments and approval linkage

evidence.observation: The approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so delegated payment actions are not inherently linked to the approving manager's reviewed record.
No audit or provenance mechanism is described that would make delegated payment actions attributable to the original approval decision.

recommendations.action: Create tamper-evident delegation logs that bind purchase request, manager approval, selected vendor, bank details, and downstream payment action into one attributable record.

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended delegation volume or removal of manual reconciliation would worsen the attribution gap.

rating.rationale: Manual validation applied from validation_checklist.md because scripts could not be run. Present inherent risk is driven by a complete authority-laundering path: trusted purchase request plus untrusted vendor quote reaches delegated irreversible payment through a peer agent that trusts the orchestrator token and receives no approval context. The declared manager approval does not earn residual credit on cap.delegate_payment because it is not wired through approval_gate_ref and does not review the delegated action. A second high present risk exists from unsigned, unpinned peer agent metadata. Forecast remains critical because adding or changing peers without structural approval-context binding or identity pinning preserves the same worst-case outcome. The control whose decay or absence most affects forecast is ctl.bind_approval_context, which is currently missing.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior or tested enforcement.
No source code, full A2A protocol transcript, or payments-agent runtime configuration was provided, so peer behavior and logging were assessed from the consumed agent card and runtime notes only.
No explicit audit logging or vendor-master implementation artifact was provided, so attribution and recipient-validation controls were treated as absent unless stated in the runtime notes.
